1	# Frade — Engineering Agent Contract
     2	
     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	This file defines repository-wide engineering rules for AI coding agents working on Frade.
     6	
     7	These rules are mandatory.
     8	
     9	Subsystem-specific rules may exist in nested `AGENTS.md` files and may impose stricter constraints.
    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	## 1. Development Method
    14	
    15	Frade uses:
    16	
    17	```text
    18	SDD / OpenSpec
    19	    ↓
    20	BDD
    21	    ↓
    22	TDD
    23	    ↓
    24	Implementation
    25	    ↓
    26	Verification
    27	    ↓
    28	Architecture Gate
    29	    ↓
    30	Archive
    31	```
    32	
    33	Implementation follows specification.
    34	
    35	Specification must not be silently changed to match implementation.
    36	
    37	Tests must not be weakened to make implementation pass.
    38	
    39	---
    40	
    41	## 2. OpenSpec Is the Change Authority
    42	
    43	For substantial product or architecture work:
    44	
    45	1. identify the active OpenSpec change;
    46	2. read its proposal/spec/design/tasks;
    47	3. validate the change before implementation;
    48	4. implement only the active scope;
    49	5. run required tests;
    50	6. run OpenSpec verification;
    51	7. pass the Architecture Gate;
    52	8. only then archive the change.
    53	
    54	Do not implement a later dependent change before the previous change has passed its gate.
    55	
    56	---
    57	
    58	## 3. STOP Conditions
    59	
    60	Stop progression whenever any of the following is true:
    61	
    62	```text
    63	required test fails
    64	typecheck fails in affected code
    65	OpenSpec validation fails
    66	OpenSpec verification has a correctness blocker
    67	architecture invariant fails
    68	architecture gate fails
    69	reference parity fails
    70	a specification conflict exists
    71	a previously fixed regression reappears
    72	```
    73	
    74	Resolve the blocker before moving to the next phase.
    75	
    76	---
    77	
    78	## 4. No Patch-Loop Rule
    79	
    80	After two unsuccessful fixes of the same deterministic defect:
    81	
    82	```text
    83	STOP PATCHING
    84	```
    85	
    86	Before another production-code modification, perform root-cause analysis.
    87	
    88	Classify the failure as:
    89	
    90	```text
    91	DOMAIN_MODEL
    92	INVARIANT
    93	ALGORITHM
    94	ABSTRACTION_BOUNDARY
    95	STATE_TRANSITION
    96	TEST
    97	SPEC_CONFLICT
    98	INTEGRATION
    99	ENVIRONMENT
   100	```
   101	
   102	Do not continue making local symptom-oriented fixes.
   103	
   104	---
   105	
   106	## 5. Regression-First Rule
   107	
   108	For a reproduced defect use:
   109	
   110	```text
   111	DEFECT
   112	 ↓
   113	DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
   114	 ↓
   115	FAILING TEST / FIXTURE
   116	 ↓
   117	ROOT CAUSE
   118	 ↓
   119	IMPLEMENTATION FIX
   120	 ↓
   121	TARGETED TEST
   122	 ↓
   123	FULL REGRESSION SUITE
   124	```
   125	
   126	Do not fix production code first and add a regression test afterwards unless reproduction before the fix is technically impossible and explicitly documented.
   127	
   128	---
   129	
   130	## 6. Test Integrity
   131	
   132	Do not make tests pass by weakening them.
   133	
   134	Forbidden without an explicit specification decision:
   135	
   136	```text
   137	test.skip
   138	it.skip
   139	describe.skip
   140	
   141	test.only
   142	it.only
   143	describe.only
   144	
   145	removing meaningful assertions
   146	loosening geometry tolerances
   147	blind snapshot regeneration
   148	deleting regression fixtures
   149	ignoring thrown errors
   150	changing expected values merely to match current implementation
   151	@ts-nocheck
   152	@ts-ignore
   153	```
   154	
   155	Existing regression tests are historical evidence.
   156	
   157	Do not remove them casually.
   158	
   159	---
   160	
   161	## 7. Architecture Direction
   162	
   163	Prefer dependency direction:
   164	
   165	```text
   166	UI / Framework
   167	      ↓
   168	Adapters
   169	      ↓
   170	Application / Interaction
   171	      ↓
   172	Domain
   173	      ↓
   174	Pure primitives
   175	```
   176	
   177	Do not solve domain defects inside renderers, React lifecycle hooks, persistence adapters, or framework glue.
   178	
   179	Fix the first incorrect decision in the proper layer.
   180	
   181	---
   182	
   183	## 8. Derived State
   184	
   185	Do not persist state that can be deterministically derived from semantic state unless the specification explicitly requires materialization.
   186	
   187	Typical transient/derived state includes:
   188	
   189	```text
   190	selection handles
   191	preview geometry
   192	render-only paths
   193	cached projections
   194	temporary interaction coordinates
   195	```
   196	
   197	---
   198	
   199	## 9. Determinism
   200	
   201	Core domain algorithms must not depend on accidental runtime state such as:
   202	
   203	```text
   204	Math.random()
   205	Date.now()
   206	DOM ordering
   207	React render ordering
   208	screen zoom
   209	devicePixelRatio
   210	pointer event frequency
   211	animation-frame timing
   212	```
   213	
   214	Identical semantic inputs must produce identical semantic outputs within the explicitly defined numeric tolerance.
   215	
   216	---
   217	
   218	## 10. Scope Discipline
   219	
   220	Do not turn an active OpenSpec change into an unrelated repository-wide refactoring.
   221	
   222	If unrelated technical debt is discovered:
   223	
   224	```text
   225	document it
   226	do not opportunistically implement it
   227	```
   228	
   229	unless it blocks the active change.
   230	
   231	---
   232	
   233	## 11. Evidence
   234	
   235	Never report:
   236	
   237	```text
   238	"should pass"
   239	"looks correct"
   240	"probably fixed"
   241	```
   242	
   243	as verification.
   244	
   245	Claims about passing tests or validation must come from commands that were actually executed.
   246	
   247	At the end of implementation report:
   248	
   249	```text
   250	CHANGE:
   251	IMPLEMENTED:
   252	FILES CHANGED:
   253	TESTS ADDED:
   254	COMMANDS EXECUTED:
   255	TEST RESULTS:
   256	KNOWN BLOCKERS:
   257	READY_FOR_VERIFY: YES | NO
   258	```
   259	
   260	---
   261	
   262	## 12. Architecture Gate
   263	
   264	An Architecture Gate is a review phase.
   265	
   266	During a gate:
   267	
   268	```text
   269	DO NOT MODIFY PRODUCTION CODE
   270	```
   271	
   272	unless the task is explicitly changed from review to repair.
   273	
   274	Gate output must contain exactly one unambiguous status:
   275	
   276	```text
   277	GATE_STATUS: PASS
   278	```
   279	
   280	or:
   281	
   282	```text
   283	GATE_STATUS: FAIL
   284	```
   285	
   286	Correctness or architecture blockers always mean `FAIL`.
   287	
   288	---
   289	
   290	## 13. No Autonomous Phase Advancement
   291	
   292	Do not automatically start the next numbered OpenSpec change after completing the current one.
   293	
   294	Example:
   295	
   296	```text
   297	R04 complete
   298	→ STOP
   299	→ report status
   300	```
   301	
   302	Do not automatically begin R05.
   303	
   304	Each numbered change is an engineering checkpoint.
   305	
   306	---
   307	
   308	## 14. Routing Engine V2
   309	
   310	Any task involving:
   311	
   312	```text
   313	edge routing
   314	edge connections
   315	terminal attachment
   316	waypoints
   317	orthogonal routing
   318	segment editing
   319	routing preview
   320	self-loops
   321	routing rendering
   322	routing/X6 integration
   323	```
   324	
   325	must additionally read:
   326	
   327	```text
   328	docs/routing-v2/drawio-routing-master-spec.md
   329	docs/routing-v2/implementation-playbook.md
   330	```
   331	
   332	These documents define the Routing Engine V2 architecture and implementation program.
   333	
   334	When a routing-specific nested `AGENTS.md` exists, its stricter rules also apply.
   335	
   336	Do not implement Routing Engine V2 from memory or from legacy code alone.
   337	
   338	---
   339	
   340	## 15. Routing V2 Sequence
   341	
   342	Routing Engine V2 follows this dependency order:
   343	
   344	```text
   345	R01 Geometry Kernel
   346	 ↓
   347	R02 Terminal / Perimeter
   348	 ↓
   349	R03 Direction Resolver
   350	 ↓
   351	R04 Orthogonal Router
   352	 ↓
   353	R05 Segment Router
   354	 ↓
   355	R06 Segment Editor
   356	 ↓
   357	R07 Preview / Commit
   358	 ↓
   359	R08 Self-loop
   360	 ↓
   361	R09 Draw.io Differential Harness
   362	 ↓
   363	R10 X6 Integration
   364	```
   365	
   366	A later change must not compensate for a defect in an earlier layer.
   367	
   368	Fix the responsible layer.
   369	
   370	---
   371	
   372	## 16. Git Safety
   373	
   374	Do not perform destructive operations merely to simplify implementation.
   375	
   376	Do not execute without explicit instruction:
   377	
   378	```text
   379	git reset --hard
   380	git clean -fd
   381	discard unrelated user changes
   382	rewrite unrelated commits
   383	```
   384	
   385	Before reporting implementation complete, inspect:
   386	
   387	```text
   388	git status
   389	git diff
   390	```
   391	
   392	Unexpected unrelated changes must be identified.
   393	
   394	---
   395	
   396	## 17. Prime Directive
   397	
   398	Do not optimize for:
   399	
   400	```text
   401	"make the current visual symptom disappear"
   402	```
   403	
   404	Optimize for:
   405	
   406	```text
   407	correct domain model
   408	+
   409	explicit invariants
   410	+
   411	deterministic implementation
   412	+
   413	executable regression protection
   414	+
   415	correct architecture boundary
   416	```
   417	
   418	---
   419	
   420	## 18. Independent Feature Ownership and Parallel Work
   421	
   422	The active change is selected for the current task and workspace. A program's
   423	`CURRENT_CHANGE.md`, phase, frozen fingerprints and numbered sequence govern work
   424	in that program; they are not a repository-wide lock on independent features.
   425	Sections 1–17 remain mandatory. A failing applicable check still stops its owner.
   426	
   427	Independent features may proceed in parallel in separate branches/worktrees.
   428	Each has its own approved scope, baseline, PRE, tests, verification, POST and
   429	archive checkpoint. Do not run concurrent writers in the same checkout. Do not
   430	copy another feature's uncommitted source, tests, dependency edits or process
   431	state into a feature workspace. Record the exact transferred files and hashes.
   432	
   433	Declare a directed dependency only when a feature consumes another feature's
   434	API, artifact or behavior. The consumer owns its waiting, integration, adapter,
   435	compatibility tests and control revalidation tasks. The supplier does not wait
   436	for the consumer's gate, completion, archive or process repair. Shared ancestry,
   437	a common package, a dirty checkout or a historical whole-file fingerprint is
   438	not by itself a product dependency.
   439	
   440	Frozen files stay frozen in the owning workspace against its approved baseline.
   441	An independent authorized change to a shared file in another workspace does not
   442	require that frozen feature's approval. When the frozen feature adopts that
   443	change, it must review the resulting control/behavior changes in its own process,
   444	preserve cumulative origin and historical evidence, and pass applicable gates
   445	before advancing. Shared-file merges are serialized; conflicts are resolved
   446	explicitly. No broad allowlist or baseline movement may conceal unauthorized work.
   447	
   448	List gate applicability by affected contract and actual feature scope. Routing
   449	V2 gates are required for routing/core or routing-contract/control work; they do
   450	not gate independent UI tokens, components, docs or UI compliance implementation.
   451	Presentation changes still require evidence that persisted/domain behavior is
   452	preserved. If a presentation change actually alters routing semantics, that
   453	change must be split into a routing-owned dependency with its required contracts
   454	and gates. Retain general repository/build/typecheck/boundary/CI requirements.
   455	
   456	Apply sequential checkpoints within each dependency chain. Independent feature
   457	chains do not acquire an ordering merely because their changes have numbers.
   458	Never report another feature's historical FAIL as the selected feature's PASS,
   459	or relabel a failing applicable check as not applicable to avoid a blocker.
   460	
   461	---
   462	
   463	## 19. Mandatory Frade UI Design Contract
   464	
   465	Every new or modified Frade UI MUST follow `docs/ui/Frade-UI-Style-Guide.md` v1.0 and the canonical shared UI tokens/components. This includes Electron, web, Draw, Repository, Projects, AI, Settings, dialogs, overlays and notifications.
   466	
   467	Read `docs/ui/Themes-and-Plugins-Spec.md` for hot-pluggable themes and native extension contracts. Light and dark ship together. Do not equate VS Code-like UX or theme import with support for all executable VS Code extensions. Every plugin contribution inherits Frade tokens, focus, keyboard and component contracts.
   468	
   469	Before a UI change:
   470	
   471	1. Read root/scoped AGENTS.md, the style guide, existing shared UI and current approved OpenSpec scope.
   472	2. Record applicable FDS/A11Y rule IDs, screens, states, theme/density coverage and keyboard contracts in the change.
   473	3. Reuse existing shared components and semantic tokens. Do not add feature-level color literals, a second visual system, an icon family or a competing theme resolver.
   474	4. Preserve VS Code workbench structure and Frade's architectural-workshop character: restored context, clear focus, beautiful diagrams, meaningful feedback on actual work.
   475	
   476	Implementation MUST stay within authorized paths. This contract does not override safety, frozen artifacts, approved domain/routing contracts or existing sequential PRE/POST gates. When an approved specification conflicts with this guide, document the exact conflict and propose a specification change through the existing workflow; do not silently reinterpret it.
   477	
   478	For every affected UI surface, verify applicable light/dark/high-contrast themes, compact/comfortable density, keyboard access, pointer targets, focus, resize/text zoom and loading/error/dirty/empty states. New behavior needs meaningful interaction coverage; cosmetic changes need appropriate visual verification, not tests that merely restate CSS.
   479	
   480	Before completion, produce a UI compliance report with PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN per applicable check, actual commands/results, commit, environment and limitations. Missing evidence MUST NOT be reported as PASS. Failed or blocked required gates prevent progression/archive under the project workflow. Baselines are not auto-approved.
   481	
   482	Changes to MUST rules, token contracts, workbench behavior or brand assets require the corresponding approved specification/ADR change. Routine choices within existing components/tokens do not require another user confirmation. The agent must not broaden a small UI task into an unrelated migration.
   483	
   484	The guide becomes binding for new changes after this section and the canonical docs are integrated. Branch/CI enforcement must be verified separately; an AGENTS instruction alone is not a technical merge protection.
   485	
   486	---
   487	
   488	## 20. Shared automatic independent reviews and branch progress
   489	
   490	These mandatory engineering rules apply to every Frade feature branch/worktree.
   491	Keep sections1–19, scoped AGENTS, approved contracts, test integrity and STOP rules.
   492	
   493	At start/resume identify the owning branch/worktree/change and Git common directory.
   494	Read the reviewed shared policy published under that common directory's
   495	frade-workflow/current.json, when present. Its content-addressed release is common
   496	to registered Frade worktrees; no account-global or per-branch reviewer setup.
   497	If a stale branch lacks the local docs/runner, load that shared release directly
   498	and record exact policy-version/hash adoption in the owning process evidence.
   499	No whole UI merge, foreign uncommitted product files or silent baseline movement.
   500	
   501	For every required PRE and POST automatically prepare a relevant authorized Frade
   502	source/contracts/tests/evidence packet, dispatch a fresh independent OpenAI Codex
   503	review using the exact model and reasoning effort assigned in the approved
   504	owning branch plan for its current stage and PRE/POST role, and receive the result. The
   505	reviewer runs in technically verified read-only packet confinement: original
   506	checkout/other-worktrees/credentials/secrets/global settings/writes/network/apps
   507	are unavailable. Authenticated harness access stays outside reviewer commands.
   508	Do not ask the human to relay prompts/results or approve each authorized review.
   509	User authorization on1October2026 extends this workflow to all Frade worktrees;
   510	other repositories and sensitive data remain excluded. Do not silently substitute
   511	a model/effort or claim an unattested backend. There is no universal model/effort
   512	default. Missing, ambiguous or conflicting stage assignments, unavailable requested
   513	models/efforts or an unverified sandbox are BLOCKED for the actual decision/limitation.
   514	Record the selected stage/role and exact plan source hash/excerpt with the review.
   515	
   516	Approved coherent plan plus validation precedes PRE; PRE PASS precedes production.
   517	Actual required tests and OpenSpec verification precede POST; POST PASS precedes

   420	## 18. Independent Feature Ownership and Parallel Work
   421	
   422	The active change is selected for the current task and workspace. A program's

   433	Declare a directed dependency only when a feature consumes another feature's
   434	API, artifact or behavior. The consumer owns its waiting, integration, adapter,

    12	### Requirement: Builtin themes and independent density
    13	
    14	The first runtime release SHALL provide offline Light, Dark and HC together, default System, explicit theme priority and independent compact/comfortable persistent density; forced-colors MUST remain system-controlled.
    15

    22

    31	
    32	All required presentation participants SHALL apply one revision without restart. Preview MUST NOT persist. Stale candidate results MUST NOT overwrite newer selection.

    32	## Decisions: resolver and durable settings
    33	
    34	1. **Resolver / registry.** Import existing generated palettes without changing them. Builtin stable IDs frade.builtin/light, frade.builtin/dark, frade.builtin/high-contrast; registry reserves these immutable offline entries. External in-memory descriptors are validated data, not installed packages. Stable publisher.name/local IDs do not depend on version/path/label. Native input accepts known role IDs and HEX6; unknown roles are diagnostic-only and never injected. Invalid values produce explicit issues without arbitrary CSS. Use all 31 roles and the existing fixed 34 contrast-pair definitions; a runtime pure constraint table must be compared to the unchanged foundation table, not diverge. Precedence builtin -> enabled selected descriptor -> user global -> selected ThemeId override -> explicitly enabled workspace override. Fixed pair order restores both roles from builtin for at most ten passes, then full builtin FALLBACK. Inputs remain unmutated; outputs/diagnostics copied and deeply frozen. Density is separate. Forced-colors final system keyword mapping overrides presentation values even with explicit Light/external overrides; do not persist system keywords as user HEX. Installed-package enable/remove/version lifecycle remains P02.
    35	
    36	2. **Persistence / startup.** One user/profile settings DTO (version 1) stored in a fixed userData presentation-settings.json, with theme System by default, preferredLight/Dark/HC IDs and density compact by default. Profile here means the existing selected Electron userData root; P07 owns multi-profile management. Opt-in workspace override is resolver data only, with no automatic workspace file reads or writes and no trust escalation. Unknown/stale IDs repair to offline builtin of kind with diagnostics, not a phantom installed theme. Main validates every DTO before and after IPC; separate channel/exposure preserves the existing window.frade health keys. Authorize the existing window/main frame/trusted page; deny child frames, forged revisions, arbitrary paths, unknown fields and oversized payloads. Serialize commits using host revision/CAS. Write a fixed-path staged file, flush and atomic rename; prepare must never replace current settings. On write failure read back authoritative state and restore old persistent/presentation selection; report unknown outcomes instead of falsely claiming rollback. Startup reads/validates before showing the window; initialize builtin/root metadata before first app paint, restore valid user selection before showing normal UI, default with visible diagnostics on malformed/unreadable settings. No repository/workspace/domain settings write, API-version rewrite or global configuration mutation.
    37	
    38	The host queue/linearization and bootstrap handshake below refine persistence; when state cannot be proven the system stays in explicit recovery rather than claiming rollback success. A synchronous renderer call reads only validated in-memory boot data, never filesystem. An external descriptor registry is in-memory data only; installing/enabling/removing packages remains P02.

   101	### B04: transaction protocol, ownership and linearization
   102	
   103	Closed states: IDLE(committed snapshot + durable host revision); PREPARING(intent,generation,membership); READY(all prepared); BARRIER_AWAIT_PAINT; APPLYING; PERSISTING (commit only); RECONCILING_UNKNOWN; COMPENSATING; PUBLISHED (preview or durable); CANCELING; RECOVERY_BLOCKED. Every message contains version1, bounded requestId, window sessionId, intent generation, transactionId, snapshot revision, membership version and exact phase. Unknown fields/roles/phase/foreign origin/source/window/frame generation reject. Payload <=32KiB and known 31 roles only. Runtime schema is separate from the existing health API.
   104	
   105	Host owns a single serialized intent/persistence queue. Renderer sends announceIntent before starting preparation; host acceptance assigns a monotonic intent generation. There is no claim that a remote user gesture cancels an already linearized OS rename before host receives it. Before each stage/rename the host verifies the current accepted generation/CAS. Once a rename has started it must be reconciled in this queue; no concurrent rename/compensation may run. The durable linearization point is successful atomic rename of the validated settings record; acknowledgement is emitted only after readback validates its transaction/generation/revision. If C arrives during A's rename, A is never published as a current UI selection: the host completes/readbacks A, then performs owned compensation or commits prepared C before allowing reveal. A cannot write after C's durable commit or acknowledgement because all these transitions share the same queue. If C preparation fails, restore the last published durable snapshot through a new host-owned compensation revision before exposing it; no old caller owns an unconstrained rollback write.
